content.text: I'll look through the comment, mention, and alert code and fix the behaviors described in the support reports.

content.thinking: The mention resolution logic likely drops oldest members when the list is truncated at 100 entries. The ordering of members in that list may be reversed.

Checking whether the notify() function deduplicates alerts.

Also examining comment.updated events, member listing order and pagination, and delete cascading. Found that listThread only attaches direct replies to top-level comments, so nested replies are missing from thread nodes despite being counted in countComments.
I will examine the comment thread UI, notify function, member list order, and event bus for adding comments.

I need to examine comment items for deleted display and event types.

Considering a per-member rate limit key for comment creation. This would require changing the bucket key to include the user ID, but getBucketConfig expects exact matches against RATE_LIMIT_BUCKETS. A mismatch would fall back to DEFAULT_BUCKET and alter capacity, potentially breaking tests.

The rate limit bug requires per-member burst tracking. I cannot change the consumeRateLimit signature without auditing all callers. The cost parameter is already taken, so adding an identity argument is not viable.

Modifying getBucketConfig to strip a user suffix is too hacky. Adding a scope discriminator to consumeRateLimit would require an actor key parameter, but the current signature only accepts orgId and bucketKey. I will check the rate limit tests before deciding how to proceed.
The duplicate alerts stem from both the action and service consuming rate limits.
Checking whether `comment.updated` exists in the event map.

I'll check the member repository for a query by email local part, or page through all members.

I'll page through members using cursors to avoid the 100-member limit. Shared handles require storing arrays of user IDs instead of a single mapping. The comment author must be excluded from mentions, and client-provided IDs should be unioned with resolved mentions.

Reply notifications require the parent comment's author.

The notification service needs to import the comment repository. The comment.created handler will look up the parent comment to identify reply recipients. Mentioned users receive comment_mention alerts. Each recipient gets at most one alert, with mention alerts taking precedence.

The comment recipient list excludes the actor and any mentioned users. Alerts are sent in two separate calls, so mentions must be filtered from the comment recipients to prevent duplicate notifications.

The new comment must be loaded to retrieve its parentId, then the parent comment loaded to identify the reply author. Deleted parent comments should still notify their author.

Rate limiting will be updated with an optional subject parameter so keys include a per-member identifier. Both the create-comment action and service currently consume rate limits for each user, which doubles the token cost per member; existing tests may expect only one consumption in the service.

The rate limit key will include the optional subject, so both the action and service consume tokens per user. This prevents one member's burst from blocking others.

The edit window will use createdAt instead of updatedAt. For comment updates, the service will re-resolve mentions from the new body, exclude the author, diff against the stored list, and emit a comment.updated event with only newly mentioned user IDs. Search can re-read the row directly.

The comment.updated event payload will carry only newly mentioned user IDs. Search listeners index on this event, and notification listeners alert those recipients with a comment_mention. The issue author is excluded from edit notifications. The updateComment repository must persist the resolved mentionedUserIds. Edit permissions already exempt allowed editors from the time limit. Mentioned inactive members are filtered out by checking active status.

Mention resolution will page through all active members in batches of 100. Invited and suspended members are excluded from mentions, while shared handles are included.

The comment thread filter `isLive` is also filtering deleted comments in the UI.

The thread UI should stop filtering archived comments so deleted placeholders remain visible. Nested replies under deleted comments must also be preserved.

The algorithm flattens all descendants under each root comment in posting order. It maps every comment to its root ancestor, groups non-root comments under those roots, and preserves archived top-level comments.

The API should return an empty body for archived comments. CommentItem already hides text when a comment is marked deleted, so blanking the body during thread mapping keeps both the API and UI consistent.

The blanked body for archived comments should be applied only in `listThread`, not in `toComment`, to avoid breaking other reads.

Comment counts already exclude archived comments, so the tree fix correctly includes nested replies in that count.

The rate limit subject parameter needs fixing.

The actor envelope for emit must include `occurredAt`.

`updateComment` must pass `mentionedUserIds` to the repository.

The repository's `updateComment` signature will accept an optional `mentionedUserIds` array. Existing callers pass only the input object, so the service will supply the new mention list explicitly.

The notification service will subscribe to `comment.updated` events. It needs the comment repository, but no circular imports exist because the comment service does not import the notification service. The handler will fetch the issue and comment by ID from the payload, then look up the parent author when a comment has a parentId.

The `comment.created` notification handler will look up the parent comment to get its author. It then gathers recipients from the issue author, assignee, and parent author while skipping duplicates and already-mentioned users. The notification is sent with the actor ID as the subject.

Tests include a rate limit mock.

Production will use the real rate limiter with an optional subject. Thread UI will stop filtering deleted comments so placeholders and replies remain visible. The list structure already nests items correctly. Empty states will show when all comments are deleted.

listThread will group descendants and strip bodies for archived comments. Cycle safety is handled. Replies and top-level comments sort by createdAt ascending.

The present function strips comment bodies for archived entries. Rate limiting will be scoped per user via actor.userId, which is backward compatible since the subject argument is optional. Service tests mock the rate limiter, but other tests may hit the real limiter and need this fix.

Both the service and action must be updated to fix rate limiting. Shared handles will appear first by their first member, then in member list order. Mention exclusion will use userId instead of handle to ensure other members are still tagged.
I will implement all edits now.

A new event could be avoided by calling the search index and notifying from the comment service.

A comment.updated listener must be added to the search service. The existing search reindex event only handles issues, so it cannot cover comments. Direct indexing during the update is unnecessary if listeners are properly registered.

Tests that call updateComment and query the search index without listeners will fail. The create path has the same dependency. Notification subscribers load via side effects when the notification service is imported. Production instrumentation ensures they are present.

Thread UI will stop filtering archived comments. Replies under deleted comments will include archived replies as placeholders. CommentItem uses isArchived for blanking, so blanking the body while preserving archivedAt works correctly. Reply counts include all non-archived replies. The rate limit manifest signature is documentation-only and does not need updating. The consumeRateLimit function will gain a fourth subject parameter.

The rate limit key now includes an optional subject parameter, defaulting to the organization and bucket when absent. Comment creation and action calls will pass actor.userId as that subject. The update repository must stringify mentioned IDs into JSON, and the service layer must supply them since the update logic always overwrites them. The author edit window uses createdAt, while non-author editors bypass it.

The author edit window will use createdAt instead of updatedAt. This prevents a user from extending their window indefinitely by repeatedly editing. Other editors changing updatedAt will not affect the author's window.

The client-provided union of mentioned user IDs will be dropped entirely. Only server-supplied mentions will be used, matching the spec exactly.

The pagination cursor type is string or null. The listMembers input accepts a nullable optional string cursor. Status values are active. A hard limit of fifty pages prevents infinite loops.

resolveMentions will skip members with an archivedAt timestamp or a non-active status. The comment thread component will stop filtering archived nodes and replies. If a thread contains only deleted comments, it will display them instead of showing an empty state.

The thread UI will use `orderThread` to determine visibility, showing an empty state only when no nodes remain. Replies will not be filtered by `isLive`. Archived comments render as `<li>` elements nested inside `<ol>`, which is valid HTML. Replies to archived top-level comments will still group under that top node.

A `threadRootId` helper will walk up a comment's parent chain to find the true thread root. If a parent is missing, the reply becomes an orphan. The spec does not define how to handle orphan replies, so they may be attached as their own top-level node.

Orphan replies will attach to the nearest existing ancestor. If no ancestor exists, they appear as top-level comments.

Orphan replies will be pushed directly as top-level roots when their parent is missing, rather than attaching to a non-existent ancestor. The present function blanks the comment body whenever archivedAt is set.
